items.title: Phrase Gym
items.text:
Phrase Gym is a local Python application with a browser interface for studying useful English phrases and keeping private recordings. Import a prepared phrase package, listen to its reference audio, record optional takes and replay them after reloading the app.

Daily offers due recall and new phrases within daily limits. First study is ungraded; on later learning days the app offers spoken recall with an honest self-rating and a scheduled return. The Library finds phrases by lesson or meaning, shows their details and saved recordings, and deletes a phrase after confirmation. The app does not claim to measure fluency.

The server works on macOS and Linux. The MVP media player and recording experience target macOS browsers. Linux browser audio qualification is planned after the MVP.

Start with installation, then import a phrase package. The service listens only on loopback and keeps learner data in its local application-data directory.

items.title: Development and releases
items.text:
Install Node 22.12+ and uv, then activate the pinned Python environment and install client tools:

. ./activate.sh
npm --prefix frontend ci
pre-commit install
cd frontend
npx playwright install chromium webkit
cd ..
inv --list

If migrating from the temporary custom hook, first run git config --unset core.hooksPath. inv pre runs the pre-commit framework, including Ruff, Pyrefly, generated-contract drift, module sizes and client formatting. Run uv run inv test for the full macOS gate. CI also runs the server tests on Linux. Tests use fake speech and silent browser audio.

inv reqs upgrades the dependency lock and pre-commit hook revisions. Review and commit both changes. inv uv installs or upgrades uv. inv docs-en serves a local documentation preview at http://127.0.0.1:8001; inv build-docs builds the site in build/docs/site/. Documentation and Allure reports are published to the gh-pages branch by their workflows. Configure GitHub Pages to serve the root of that branch. CI also provides coverage comments, Codecov and Coveralls integration; external coverage services require their repository setup.

items.title: Build a distributable
items.text:
uv run inv build

This builds the Vue client into src/phrase_gym/server/static/ before the Python wheel and source distribution. Do not publish a wheel built from an outdated client. src/phrase_gym/__about__.py is the package-version source; Hatch reads it for both distributions.

inv build-frontend rebuilds only the Vue client. inv run --build builds the client and starts the server; inv run starts the server with the existing client build. Pre-commit contains the Ruff configuration and runs Pyrefly directly. Invoke provides the build, test and server tasks.

items.title: Private Tailscale access
items.text:
With Tailscale already connected, run inv run --build --tailscale. The task points the existing HTTPS Serve route at 127.0.0.1:8000 and passes the exact machine origin to Phrase Gym. The backend remains on loopback; only devices permitted by your Tailscale policy can use this shared library. This does not enable public Funnel access. Run Coach with PHRASE_GYM_PIPER_CONFIG when preparing text-only material. The server starts without Piper and continues to serve study and replay while Coach is stopped.

Use tailscale serve status to inspect the route. Stop an old Phrase Gym process before starting the replacement; retain its data directory and recordings. On iPhone, use the HTTPS machine URL with Tailscale connected. Microphone permission and actual playback still need attended checks.

items.title: Publish a release
items.text:
From a clean main synchronized with origin/main, choose an increment:

inv version
inv ver-bug --dry-run
inv ver-bug       # patch
inv ver-feature   # minor
inv ver-release   # major

The version task asks for confirmation, updates the version and uv.lock, runs the local gates, commits, creates an annotated vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH tag, and atomically pushes the branch and tag. The tag workflow verifies tag/version agreement, runs CI for that exact tag, builds the package, publishes to PyPI using PYPI_USERNAME and PYPI_PASSWORD repository secrets, and creates a GitHub release with the same tag. Ordinary branch pushes do not publish a package.

scripts/verup.sh ss prints a PEP 440 snapshot identifier without publishing. scripts/verup_action.sh retains the scaffold's shortened-tag helper; major/minor tags are not package releases. Use the Invoke commands above for PyPI releases. Restoring or testing this tooling does not itself create a release tag.

items.title: Importing prepared English phrases
items.text: Phrase Gym accepts one UTF-8 JSON object. Import format phrase-gym.package version 2 is the current package contract; earlier versions are rejected. The application makes no model or course-provider call during import; source links are attribution only and are never fetched.

items.title: Schema
items.text:
Field Requirement format Exactly phrase-gym.package version Exactly 2; other versions fail clearly package_id Stable ID for this exact package content; letters, digits, ., _, - source_id Stable identity for the course/unit/source source_label Short learner-readable attribution source_link Optional absolute HTTP(S) attribution URL learning_language en card_language en help_language en lessons 1–20 lessons with at most 50 phrases in total; an ordinary batch has 5–10 phrases

All reference audio for one package, whether Coach prepares it or an agent supplies it, must fit one 9 MiB budget: about 3.5 minutes of speech at 22,050 Hz. Fifty long sentences can exceed it; the import then fails with an error asking you to split the package, so keep packages short.

Each lesson has a stable lesson_id, a learner-readable title and one or more phrases. One package may contain several lessons; every phrase belongs to exactly one of them.

Each phrase requires:

Field Requirement item_id Stable ID, unique within the package text The fixed complete English wording explanation Short English meaning/use help shown after the answer cues One or two distinct situations; each has situation and an optional partner_line recall_hints Two to six distinct hand-prepared hints of one or two words, at most 40 characters each, never the whole phrase usage_contexts One to six distinct short searchable uses, such as small talk or greetings accepted_variants Optional genuinely suitable alternatives for the same intention detailed_explanation Optional longer native-language help shown on request

Unknown fields are rejected, and validation names the lesson, phrase and field to correct.

source_id plus lesson_id is permanent lesson identity: a later package can add phrases to that lesson only with the same title. source_id plus item_id is permanent phrase identity. Repeating it while that phrase is in the Library is rejected without overwriting it. To replace a defective phrase, delete it in the Library or its details after confirmation, then import the corrected phrase in a new package; it becomes a new phrase with fresh reference audio.

The generated machine-readable request schema is available at frontend/openapi.json. A complete three-lesson file is examples/meeting-phrases.json.

items.title: Instruction for an external preparation agent
items.text:
Prepare 5–10 useful fixed English phrases from the supplied course material as one Phrase Gym package version 2. Preserve the course wording, group phrases into the course's lessons, and give the package, source, every lesson and every phrase a stable searchable ID. For each phrase provide the complete English text, a short plain-English meaning/use explanation, one or two distinct short situations that communicate the intention without revealing the target wording, two or more hand-picked recall hints of one or two words that help retrieve this exact wording (not simply its first or last word), and short usage_contexts a learner might search for. Add a preceding partner line only when natural. Include only genuinely acceptable variants. Use the "So far, so good." phrase in the example file as the model. Do not add raw words, variable slots, dialogue graphs, invented quotations, audio URLs, or fields outside the documented schema. Return JSON only, then inspect every phrase for intended meaning, natural cues, answer leakage, useful hints and contexts, and suitable alternatives before giving it to the learner.

Phrase Gym validates structure, not teaching quality. The learner or a semantic reviewer still checks real prepared content separately.

items.title: Piper voice
items.text:
The separately running Coach expects PHRASE_GYM_PIPER_CONFIG to name a private JSON file outside the repository. Piper itself is a separately pinned environment.

On the learner's macOS machine, create that private environment outside every repository with the same Python minor version as Phrase Gym and these exact packages:

PIPER="$HOME/Library/Application Support/io.github.andgineer.Phrase-Gym/piper-1.8.0"
python3.13 -m venv "$PIPER"
"$PIPER/bin/python" -I -m pip install --no-deps --only-binary=:all: \
  piper-tts==1.8.0 onnxruntime==1.31.0 flatbuffers==25.12.19 numpy==2.5.4 \
  packaging==25.0 pathvalidate==3.3.1 protobuf==7.36.2
"$PIPER/bin/python" -I -m pip check

Download the selected model and adjacent JSON configuration outside the repository, calculate both SHA-256 values, and create the private voice file with this shape:

{
  "executable": "/absolute/path/to/piper/bin/python",
  "runtime_version": "1.8.0",
  "model": "/absolute/path/to/en_US-ljspeech-medium.onnx",
  "model_sha256": "64-lowercase-hex-digits",
  "config": "/absolute/path/to/en_US-ljspeech-medium.onnx.json",
  "config_sha256": "64-lowercase-hex-digits",
  "voice": "en_US-ljspeech-medium",
  "locale": "en-US"
}

Coach verifies the exact installed piper-tts version against runtime_version, model/config hashes, and English locale. It streams the selected interpreter's output under hard 8 MiB audio, 64 KiB diagnostic, and 60-second limits, terminates a process that exceeds a bound, and sends WAV references to the Phrase Gym API for atomic publication. Automated tests use a silent fake child and never invoke real Piper.

items.title: API handoff
items.text:
POST /api/imports accepts { "package": <version-2 package> }. The server validates and stores a text-only request before returning pending. Start phrase-gym coach separately to prepare it. GET /api/imports and GET /api/imports/{package_id} report pending, preparing, added, or error. Retry an error or interrupted preparation with POST /api/imports/{package_id}/retry; retrying the same package content returns its existing status. Coach retrieves work and returns a complete result through the API; it never opens the application database.

An external agent that already has audio can call POST /api/imports with package and references, a map from each item_id to base64-encoded mono 16-bit PCM WAV bytes. Every phrase must have one complete playable reference, at most 8 MiB, and all references together must fit a 9 MiB audio budget. These limits keep the base64 JSON below the API's 16 MiB request limit. This publishes the batch atomically and returns added without Coach. A malformed or missing reference identifies the item and rejects the whole request. Retrying identical package and audio returns the original result; changed content under the same package_id is rejected. The browser paste/file import accepts text-only packages and shows pending Coach work while it is offline.

items.title: Installation and launch
items.text:
Use Python 3.13 and uv. Published packages include the built browser client:

uv tool install phrase-gym --upgrade --python 3.13

Until a release is published, install from a source checkout:

uv sync --frozen
npm --prefix frontend ci
npm --prefix frontend run build

Configure a local English Piper voice, then start the server:

PHRASE_GYM_PIPER_CONFIG=/absolute/path/to/piper-voice.json phrase-gym run

For a source checkout, use uv run phrase-gym run instead. Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. Use phrase-gym run --help for the port and data-directory options. Keep voice files and learner recordings outside the source checkout. Actual microphone and headset acceptance requires attended testing on the learner's MacBook.

The coach command is present but preparation is pending the API handoff. The install-coach, uninstall-coach, and deploy commands report that they are unavailable. The coach extra supplies Piper; deploy is reserved for later provisioning. The core server and help need only the lean installation.

items.title: Python API reference
items.text: The HTTP contract is generated from the Python models. A running server exposes it at /openapi.json and its interactive API documentation at /docs.

items.title: phrase_gym.server.import_contracts.PhrasePackage
items.text:
Bases: StrictModel

Source code in src/phrase_gym/server/import_contracts.py 
class PhrasePackage(StrictModel):
    format: Literal["phrase-gym.package"]
    version: Literal[2]
    package_id: str = Field(pattern=IDENTITY_PATTERN)
    source_id: str = Field(pattern=IDENTITY_PATTERN)
    source_label: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=200)
    source_link: HttpUrl | None = None
    learning_language: Literal["en"]
    card_language: Literal["en"]
    help_language: Literal["en"]
    lessons: list[ImportLesson] = Field(min_length=1, max_length=20)

    @field_validator("lessons")
    @classmethod
    def identities_are_unique(cls, lessons: list[ImportLesson]) -> list[ImportLesson]:
        lesson_ids = [lesson.lesson_id for lesson in lessons]
        if len(lesson_ids) != len(set(lesson_ids)):
            raise ValueError("lesson_id values must be unique within a package")
        item_ids = [phrase.item_id for lesson in lessons for phrase in lesson.phrases]
        if len(item_ids) != len(set(item_ids)):
            raise ValueError("phrase item_id values must be unique within a package")
        if len(item_ids) > MAX_PACKAGE_PHRASES:
            raise ValueError(f"a package may contain at most {MAX_PACKAGE_PHRASES} phrases")
        return lessons

    def phrases(self) -> list[tuple[ImportLesson, ImportPhrase]]:
        return [(lesson, phrase) for lesson in self.lessons for phrase in lesson.phrases]

items.title: phrase_gym.server.app.create_app()
items.text:
Source code in src/phrase_gym/server/app.py 
def create_app() -> FastAPI:
    remote_origin = os.environ.get("PHRASE_GYM_TAILSCALE_ORIGIN", "")
    data_dir = Path(os.environ.get("PHRASE_GYM_DATA_DIR", ".data")).resolve()
    database = Database(data_dir)
    cleanup = FileCleanup(database)
    cleanup.retry()
    app = FastAPI(title="Phrase Gym", version="1.0.0")
    app.state.database = database
    importer = Importer(database)
    app.state.importer = importer
    app.include_router(import_routes(importer))
    app.include_router(coach_routes(importer))
    app.include_router(recording_routes(RecordingStore(database)))
    app.state.daily = DailyPractice(database)
    app.state.view_actions = ViewActions(database)
    app.state.completion = PracticeCompletion(database)
    app.include_router(
        practice_routes(app.state.daily, app.state.view_actions, app.state.completion),
    )
    library = LibraryService(database)
    lessons = LessonChoices(database)
    app.state.lessons = lessons
    app.include_router(library_routes(library, lessons))
    app.include_router(deletion_routes(PhraseDeletion(database, cleanup)))
    app.include_router(settings_routes(SettingsService(database)))
    app.add_middleware(LocalBoundary, tailscale_origin=remote_origin)
    app.add_middleware(
        TrustedHostMiddleware,
        allowed_hosts=trusted_hosts(remote_origin),
    )

    @app.get("/api/health")
    def health() -> dict[str, str]:
        return {"status": "ok"}

    static = Path(__file__).parent / "static"
    if static.is_dir():
        app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory=static, html=True), name="client")
    return app
